profile.campus: Google Council Bluffs, Pottawattamie County, IA
profile.address: Halley Street, Google Data Center, Council Bluffs, Lewis Township, Pottawattamie County, IA (3)
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's Council Bluffs, Iowa data center campus, mapped along Halley Street in Lewis Township, Pottawattamie County, one of several OSM-mapped buildings on this street. Google's own locations page for Iowa, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within the campus, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived street location.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Iowa data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the Council Bluffs campus was the site of Google's original $600 million Iowa investment announced in 2007, and that the company has since invested more than $20 billion in the state; in 2025 Google announced a further $7 billion investment shared between an expanded Council Bluffs campus and a new Cedar Rapids facility. Google reports generating $2.7 billion of economic activity for Iowa businesses in 2025 and training over 112,000 Iowans in digital skills through its Grow with Google partnerships.

The Council Bluffs campus has grown into one of Google's largest data center clusters globally over nearly two decades of continuous expansion, though Google's own public materials describe the campus in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings, addresses, or per-building capacity figures.

MidAmerican Energy, the principal electric utility serving Council Bluffs, has pursued a long-running commitment to source renewable wind generation for its Iowa customers, a factor Google has cited in its own public materials as part of the state's appeal for data center investment. Iowa's data center-specific sales tax exemption on qualifying equipment and electricity, administered at the state level, has been credited by state economic development officials with helping draw and retain large-scale data center investment in the state, including from Microsoft and Meta, both separately tracked in this registry.

profile.capacity_note: Google does not publish a megawatt IT capacity figure for any individual Council Bluffs building; third-party data center trackers (not Google's own disclosures) have estimated the overall Council Bluffs campus in the range of 100-300+ MW across its full build-out, a figure this entry does not adopt as fact because it is not operator-confirmed.
profile.facility_note: Google has not published a building-specific name, street address, or square footage for this individual structure within its Council Bluffs campus; this entry is one of the OSM-mapped buildings within that campus footprint, distinguished from its neighbors only by street (Vostok, McMurdo, Halley, Orcadas, Palmer, Concordia, or Bancroft Street) and coordinate.

profile.regional_context: Council Bluffs sits directly across the Missouri River from Omaha, Nebraska, and Google's Iowa data center operations (Council Bluffs, and more recently Cedar Rapids) are served primarily by MidAmerican Energy, which has pursued a long-running commitment to source renewable wind generation for its Iowa customers, a factor frequently cited in Google's own siting rationale for the state. Iowa's data center-specific sales tax exemption on equipment and electricity, administered at the state level, has been credited by state officials with helping draw and retain large-scale data center investment including Google, Microsoft, and Meta, all separately tracked in this registry.

reading.body:
Google's Council Bluffs campus in Pottawattamie County is part of a regional facility established in 2007 that Google has now invested over $20 billion in across Iowa, with a $7 billion expansion announced for Council Bluffs and a new Cedar Rapids site. The company does not publish megawatt capacity, square footage, or exact addresses for individual buildings at this campus, only aggregate state-level figures. Google has tied regional power strategy to a NextEra Energy agreement to restart Iowa's Duane Arnold nuclear plant.

Among the 52 mapped data center facilities in Iowa, only two publish power capacity figures, totaling 18 MW in disclosed capacity statewide. This campus ranks third by published megawatts in the state, meaning at least two other disclosed facilities have more capacity. The absence of a published figure for Council Bluffs makes its actual scale relative to other Iowa sites unknown and prevents direct comparison to the state's disclosed capacity total.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI infrastructure, the unpublished specifications mean the decision cannot rest on engineering data. The scale signal comes instead from Google's $20 billion regional investment, the announced $7 billion expansion, and the company's tie to nuclear generation restarts, which together indicate sustained capital commitment to this location as a major compute destination. Whether that translates to AI workload density or merely to broader Google services cannot be determined from public data.
